The Author in Portrait

The woman behind the words

Before the books, there is the woman who lived them. These portraits show Laketha as her readers meet her: warm, assured, and entirely herself. In the second, she holds Redemptions Journey, the volume that carries the story of Redemption forward. Two newer portraits join them below, one full length in a bright chevron skirt before a red telephone box, and one close and joyful selfie.

Her full story, the study, the service, and the writing, is told in About the Author, and both books are presented in full in The Books.

The Books

One story, two volumes

Read in order, the two books form a single arc: first the story of a woman brought low and lifted up, then the longer, quieter work of walking out that redemption day by day. Each stands on its own. Together, they are a testimony.

The actual cover.
A yellow rose rises where sorrow has been; monarch butterflies, emblems of transformation, circle a figure still bound by thorns.

Book One: The Story

Redemption: The Story of a Woman

“What breaks is not the end of the story.”

Published 2020Book OneWrite by Faith PublicationsAvailable on Amazon

Laketha Hicks’s debut is the foundation of her work as an author: a woman’s story, told plainly and without flinching. It is a book about the seasons that undo us, the losses, the detours, the moments when the life we planned gives way beneath us, and about the grace that meets a woman precisely there.

What gives the book its power is its honesty. Redemption here is not presented as a slogan or a sudden rescue. It is rendered as something real, costly, and deeply personal: the slow discovery that a woman’s worth is not decided by her worst chapter, and that faith can hold even when circumstances do not cooperate.

Readers who have known disappointment, grief, or the quiet work of starting over will recognise themselves in these pages and will find, in the telling, both companionship and courage.

Within these pages

  • A testimony, not a performance: a story told with candour, in the voice of a woman who has lived what she writes.
  • Faith under pressure: belief examined in the hard seasons, not only celebrated in the easy ones.
  • The beginning of the arc: the moment of change that its sequel, Redemptions Journey, then carries forward.

Book Two: The Journey

Redemptions Journey

“Being set free is the beginning. Learning to walk free is the journey.”

Published 2022Book TwoWrite by Faith PublicationsAvailable on Amazon

Two years after Redemption, Laketha returned with its continuation, and the shift in the title tells you everything. The first book is about the moment: the breaking and the rescue. Redemptions Journey is about everything that comes after: the daily, deliberate work of healing, growing, and becoming.

This is a book for the reader who has survived the crisis and now faces the harder question: what does a redeemed life actually look like on an ordinary Tuesday? With the same candour that marked her debut, Laketha writes about perseverance, about faith practised rather than merely professed, and about a woman learning to inhabit her freedom fully.

Read together, the two volumes offer something rare: not just inspiration for a moment, but companionship for a road.

Within these pages

  • The walk after the rescue: healing and growth treated as a journey, not an event.
  • Faith for the long road: perseverance, discipline, and hope for the seasons when change feels slow.
  • The completion of the arc: the natural second volume for every reader who found herself in Book One.

How to read them

Start with Redemption: The Story of a Woman (2020), then continue with Redemptions Journey (2022). The first book tells the story; the second walks it out. Either can be read on its own, but together they trace the full arc from breaking to blooming, which is exactly what their covers, placed side by side, depict: thorns and butterflies first, then blossoms and freedom.

✦
The Covers

Art that tells the story first

Before a single page is turned, the two covers preach the sermon. Read side by side, they form a diptych: bondage and bloom, thorn and blossom, the whole theology of Laketha’s writing rendered in image.

Redemption: The Story of a Woman

Black, white, and one defiant yellow: a study in sorrow and stubborn hope.

  • The yellow roseWhere her face should be, a rose in full bloom: beauty and identity restored, rising out of suffering rather than apart from it.
  • The thorn vinesBarbed stems cross her back like bindings: the pain, shame, and circumstance a woman can find herself wrapped in.
  • The monarch butterfliesNature’s emblem of metamorphosis drifts at either side: transformation is already in the air, even while the thorns remain.
  • The dark poolShe kneels in black water, low but not lost: the posture of a woman at the turning point of her story.

Redemptions Journey

Darkness again, but this time she is standing, moving, and the vines are in flower.

  • The emerald gownShe stands now, dressed in deep green, the colour of living, growing things, no longer kneeling, but mid stride.
  • The breaking vinesThe thorns that bound her in Book One are in her hands and snapping at her wrists: freedom here is active, seized, and walked in.
  • The flowering branchesThe very thicket that imprisoned her erupts in pink and yellow blossom: the past is not erased; it is redeemed, and made to bloom.
  • The lifted headHer silhouette is bright against the dark: a woman no longer defined by what held her, but by where she is going.
Themes

What her writing returns to

Four threads run through both books, the same four threads that run through Laketha’s life of study, leadership, and service.

01

Faith

Belief as an anchor rather than an ornament, trusted most precisely when the season is hardest and the outcome least visible.

02

Resilience

The refusal to let hardship have the final word: strength that bends, grieves, and still gets up the next morning.

03

Healing

Honest room for grief and growth alike: restoration treated as a process to be honoured, never a performance to be rushed.

04

Purpose

What comes after redemption: a life of intention and service, in which what was survived becomes what is offered to others.

For book clubs & reading circles

These are books that ask to be discussed. Their themes, faith tested, identity restored, freedom learned slowly, open naturally into conversation, which makes the pair a rewarding choice for book clubs, women’s groups, and faith communities.

Read Book One together, then take up the Journey a month later, or work through the questions here after either volume.

Invite a conversation
  1. Beginnings. What does “redemption” mean to you, and did the book change that definition?
  2. The thorns. The covers show a woman bound by vines. What are the “thorns” women carry most quietly, and why do they go unspoken?
  3. Moment vs. journey. Why does change so often arrive as a process rather than an event? Where have you seen that in your own life?
  4. Faith under pressure. What sustains belief when circumstances give it nothing to stand on?
  5. Blooming anyway. In the second cover, the imprisoning vines burst into flower. What might it mean for a painful past to be redeemed rather than erased?
  6. Walking free. What is one practice, daily, unglamorous, faithful, that helps a person live out a new chapter?
✦
About the Author

A leader who writes, a writer who leads

Laketha’s authority on the page comes from a full life off it: family and faith, two master’s degrees earned with honours, and nearly two decades of operational leadership in one of Alabama’s largest hospitals.

From Harvest, Alabama, with purpose

Laketha Hicks makes her home in Harvest, Alabama, in the Huntsville and Madison community she has served for most of her professional life. Since 2007 she has served as Coordinator of Operations for Environmental Services at Huntsville Hospital, the second largest hospital in Alabama, coordinating operations for the main campus and for Huntsville Hospital for Women & Children, and supporting affiliated hospitals across North Alabama, including Madison, Athens Limestone, Helen Keller, and Decatur.

It is work that happens largely out of sight and matters enormously: the cleanliness, safety, and readiness of the spaces where patients heal and families wait. Laketha leads teams, trains and mentors staff, resolves conflict, and answers to senior leadership for standards that cannot slip. That she has been recognised with Superior Performance Ratings for fifteen consecutive years speaks to a rare consistency. Colleagues and executives alike know her for an exceptional work ethic, personal accountability, and genuine care for the people her work touches.

Alongside that career, she pursued scholarship with the same tenacity: an accounting degree from Alabama A&M University, then an MBA and an MPA from Florida Institute of Technology, both Magna cum Laude, followed by doctoral coursework in business administration at Walden University. Few authors bring both a boardroom tested understanding of organisations and a hospital floor understanding of people in crisis. Laketha brings both, and it shows in the practicality of her hope.

That is why redemption, in her hands, is never an abstraction. It is daily work: showing up, telling the truth, extending grace, and beginning again, in a hospital corridor, in a classroom, and on the page.

Reader Questions

Frequently asked questions

Answers readers ask most often, about buying the books, reading them in order, and reading them together.

Where can I buy Laketha’s books? +

Both books are available on Amazon. Use the “Shop on Amazon” buttons on the Books page. Each goes directly to that book’s Amazon page, where you will find the current format, edition, and price.

Which book should I read first? +

Begin with Redemption: The Story of a Woman (2020), then continue with Redemptions Journey (2022). The second book builds directly on the first: story first, then the journey that follows it.

Are the two books a series? +

Yes. They form an arc in two volumes from the same author and publisher. Each can be read on its own, but together they trace a complete movement: the moment of redemption, and then the lifelong walk that follows.

Who publishes her books? +

Both books were published by Write by Faith Publications, as recorded on Laketha’s résumé and shown on the covers themselves.

Can our book club or group read them together? +

Absolutely. The books were written to be shared and discussed. You will find discussion questions prepared for you on the Books page, and you are warmly invited to write to Laketha using the email on the Contact page.

How can I contact Laketha about her books? +

By email at laketha.hicks@gmail.com, for reader messages, book clubs, and speaking or community enquiries.

From Laketha

Words from her heart

Reflections on faith, on beginning again, and on the journey behind her books. Begin with these three posts, and look for new pieces from Laketha here.

November 12, 2026

Faith for the Season You Are In

Faith is not only for the days when the answer is clear. It is for the mornings when you pray and still have to wait, and you choose to trust God in the waiting.

I have learned that faith is not only for the days when the answer is clear. Faith is for the mornings when you pray and still have to wait. It is for the hospital corridor and the quiet kitchen, for the moments when nobody sees you holding it together but God.

There were seasons when I wanted God to move quickly, and instead He taught me to stand firmly. Standing is still faith. Waiting is still faith. Getting up one more time and doing the next right thing, that is faith too.

If you are in a waiting season, I want you to hear this from my heart. God has not forgotten you. The silence is not absence. Keep praying, keep serving, keep believing, and watch how He meets you, one honest step at a time.

October 28, 2026

Beginning Again Is Not Failure

Beginning again does not mean you failed. It means you lived, you learned, and by grace you still have the courage to start where you are and build something honest.

Beginning again does not mean you failed. It means you lived. It means you learned some things the hard way, and by grace you still have breath in your body and courage in your heart to start where you are.

I know what it is to look at a chapter and wish you could rewrite it. You cannot go back, but you can begin again, wiser this time, softer in the right places and stronger in the places that matter. A new beginning rarely looks grand. Most days it looks like one small faithful choice, and then another.

So do not let shame name your next chapter. Let faith name it. You are not starting from nothing. You are starting from experience, and God is able to make even that fruitful.

October 14, 2026

Why I Wrote Redemption and Redemptions Journey

I wrote Redemption because I knew I was not the only woman who had been broken by a season and wondered whether God could put her life back together. The Journey came because healing takes time.

I wrote Redemption: The Story of a Woman because I knew I was not the only woman who had been broken by a season and wondered whether God could put her life back together. That first book is the story. It tells the truth about the breaking, and it tells the truth about the grace that met me there.

Redemptions Journey came two years later because I learned that being set free is only the beginning. After the rescue comes the walk. After the tears come the daily choices. The second book is for the woman who survived the hard chapter and now asks, Lord, how do I live free, day by day?

If my books do anything, I pray they sit with a woman the way a good friend would, honest and kind, and remind her that her story is not over. There is more to your story, and God is still writing.
